# import-boundaries (KIB001)

**Forbidden import boundaries**

This rule is enabled by default.

## What it does

Checks direct imports against configured forbidden module-prefix boundaries.

## Why is this bad?

A reusable package that imports feature or test-suite code becomes coupled to implementation details that should depend on it, not the other way around.

## Options

Configured in `[tool.konform.lint.import-boundaries]`.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source-roots` | `string list` | ["src", "."] | Python import roots relative to the config file. |
| `forbidden` | `boundary list` | [] | One-way importing and target module-prefix pairs to reject. |
| `allowed` | `boundary list` | [] | Reviewed importing/target prefix pairs exempt from both KIB rules. |
| `level` | `string` | "warning" | Violation level: warning or error. |

## Suppression

```python
x = 1  # noqa: KIB001
x = 1  # noqa: KIB  (every KIB* rule)
```
